title: GADGETSPINNER: A New Transient Execution Primitive Using the Loop Stream Detector
problem: Modern out-of-order CPUs have unexploited transient execution vulnerabilities in the Loop Stream Detector (LSD), which retains stale branch predictions across loop iterations and enables speculative out-of-bounds execution and information leakage.
motivation: Transient execution attacks are a critical security threat to all modern CPUs, and existing transient execution defenses fail against LSD-based attacks.
method: GADGETSPINNER exploits the Loop Stream Detector's behavior of holding old branch predictions from the first loop iteration and reusing them until a branch misprediction resolves. This creates a transient execution window between speculative out-of-loop-bounds execution and misprediction resolution where illegal operations execute and leak confidential information.
key_novelty: First transient execution primitive exploiting the Loop Stream Detector's reuse of stale branch predictions across loop iterations to enable speculative out-of-bounds execution.
